chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali and Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Ja'far ibn Sama'ah, all from Hammad ibn 'Uthman from Zurarah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said:
The representation (agency) is not valid in the divorce.

key_terms.الوَكَالَةُ: Agency or representation (delegating an act to another)

ai.seo_question: Is delegation allowed for pronouncing divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the principle that divorce is a personal act requiring the husband's direct pronouncement, thereby invalidating delegation to an agent (wakalah). This ruling underscores the gravity of talaq as a unilateral decree that cannot be mediated through proxy, distinguishing it from other contractual acts in Shia jurisprudence. It reflects the scholarly consensus on the necessity of the husband's presence and intent for the validity of the divorce pronouncement.
